original_test_intent: Observe the NVLink indicator through cable-absent boot, cable-present stress, live hotplug and cable-present AC-on transitions, including the missing locate-command Amber Blink state.
original_method: A qualified hardware operator follows an approved topology-specific cable and AC sequence, runs the pinned nvqual item 8 workload, records the indicator continuously, and restores and verifies every NVLink path.
manual_activity: An ESD-qualified operator verifies the exact NVLink cable endpoints, executes the approved cold and live sequences plus pinned nvqual stress, records continuous LED video and fabric telemetry, then restores full topology.
required_inputs: Exact GPU/NVSwitch/port/cable topology and LED-to-link mapping
Cable PN/revision, insertion/removal sequence, discharge and ESD controls
Platform statement that live NVLink hotplug is supported for this configuration
Pinned nvqual package, item 8 command, workload duration and pass/error/thermal limits
Authoritative confirmation that no green blink during stress is expected
Authoritative confirmation that amber must not appear during hotplug or boot
NVIDIA locate command, supported target syntax and Amber Blink cadence
AC control, maintenance window, workload quiescence and independent recovery
safety_requirements: Never remove or insert an NVLink cable until topology, supported service state and ESD procedure are confirmed
Treat live hotplug as prohibited unless platform engineering explicitly approves it
Quiesce dependent GPU workloads and prove fabric redundancy or maintenance isolation
Do not guess nvqual item numbering or an NVIDIA locate command
Stop on connector resistance, latch damage, unexpected link loss, GPU/Xid/fabric error, power or thermal anomaly
Do not automatically repeat cable, stress or AC operations
agent_execution_scope: Verify source and approved topology/artifact inputs
Collect read-only GPU, NVLink, NVSwitch, error, thermal and power baselines
Prepare synchronized stimulus/video/telemetry timeline and validate operator-supplied artifacts
Collect post-restoration health and compare link identities
Perform no AC transition, cable handling, hotplug, stress start, locate action, retry, visual judgment or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve physical topology, cable procedure, live-hotplug support and recovery
Pin nvqual item 8 and define limits
Confirm negative blink/amber expectations and supply locate command semantics
Review continuous visual and fabric evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL CRITICAL NVLINK PHYSICAL/POWER TEST REQUIRES TOPOLOGY-SPECIFIC INTERLOCKS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Instrument the exact link endpoints, record continuous indicator video, align each frame to AC/cable/stress events and NVLink state/error telemetry, and restore the full fabric after each separately authorized scenario.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds topology identity, hotplug authorization, artifact pinning, measurable timing/limits, aborts and independent recovery without rewriting source expectations.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Telemetry can prove link and workload state but cannot establish visible LED behavior; locate-based Amber Blink is still untestable until NVIDIA supplies the command.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: NVLink is a high-speed fabric with topology dependencies; a cable action can partition peer GPUs or propagate workload errors. A green aggregate LED may also stay lit for a surviving link, so endpoint-level counters are required to know which path was exercised.

project_override_considerations: If live cable service is unsupported, preserve that source scenario as BLOCKED or revision-scoped N/A; do not silently replace it with a cold-plug test because that removes coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and unique-code result
Approved topology, cable identity, service-state and recovery documents
Pinned nvqual item 8 artifact/command, limits and complete output
Continuous contextual/close LED video synchronized to AC, cable, hotplug and stress events
Pre/during/post endpoint NVLink/NVSwitch state, counters, errors, Xids, thermal and power evidence
Locate-command disposition, no-unapproved-hotplug/no-auto-retry audit, restored topology and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure explicitly states negative behavior under Green Blink and Amber Solid headings. Although counterintuitive and requiring confirmation, it does not provide a second competing expected value.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Defined cold/stress observations can be prepared after approval; unsupported live hotplug or missing locate command may block individual scenarios and must be recorded without invalidating this static review.

review_improvement: Adds exact fabric identity, live-service interlocks, pinned stress semantics, synchronized endpoint evidence and restoration proof while retaining every original negative and unresolved state.
independent_technical_reasoning: NVLink cable state is meaningful only for a named pair of endpoints and link instances; aggregate GPU health can stay green while one fabric edge is absent or retrains. Continuous link-state and error counters must therefore be synchronized with the physical LED and cable event. Because live cable manipulation can create asymmetric training and workload faults, cold removal and hotplug are distinct coverage and cannot substitute for each other.
